questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: How is '1 peg' defined at the top of the chapter?
questions.exp: '1 peg = 60 ml Alcohol (40%)'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: Cirrhogenic dose — match — 1) Male 2) Female … A) 20–40 gm/day (1 peg) B) 40–80 g/day (2 pegs)
questions.exp: Male: 40–80 g/day (2 pegs); Female: 20–40 gm/day (1 peg). (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: The cirrhogenic dose must be consumed for how long to produce cirrhosis?
questions.exp: '→ 5 days a week for 15 years → Cirrhosis.' (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: Alcoholic hepatitis: printed mortality and best serum marker?
questions.exp: 'Mortality 70%' and 'Best Serum marker : Carbohydrate deficient transferrin'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: In the progression diagram, alcohol consumption leads to alcoholic fatty liver after how long, and is that stage reversible?
questions.exp: 'Alcohol Consumption —3–5 years→ Alcoholic fatty liver (Reversible)'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: From the fatty-liver branch point, judge: I Cirrhosis begins micronodular and progresses to macronodular. II In macronodular cirrhosis the nucleus is pushed to the periphery. III Cirrhosis carries risk of HCC.
opts: I true, II and III false
II and III true, I false
I and III true, II false
questions.exp: Cirrhosis → micronodular → Progress → macronodular (Nucleus pushed to periphery); → Risk of HCC. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: The other branch from alcoholic fatty liver is alcoholic hepatitis (high mortality). What cause is printed beneath it?
questions.exp: 'Alcoholic hepatitis (High mortality) — Cause : Binge drinking'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: Alcohol metabolism — which of the following is NOT one of the three enzymes branched in the diagram?
questions.exp: Enzyme: Aldehyde dehydrogenase; Cyt P2E1; Catalase. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: Fill up the pathway: Alcohol → ______ (toxic to liver) —aldehyde dehydrogenase→ metabolic products.
questions.exp: 'Alcohol → Acetaldehyde —Aldehyde dehydrogenase→ metabolic products'; 'Acetaldehyde → Toxic to liver'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: Peg, cirrhogenic dose, alcoholic hepatitis mortality/marker, progression diagram, alcohol metabolism
questions.q: Two men drink identically; one carries an aldehyde-dehydrogenase polymorphism making him a poor metaboliser. Per the diagram, what is his particular risk?
opts: Higher carbohydrate-deficient transferrin but no liver risk
Protected, because less acetaldehyde is formed
questions.exp: Polymorphism → Efficient metaboliser / Poor metaboliser: 'Prone to develop alcohol hepatitis'. (Book p1026)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Fill up: The adverse-effects mnemonic printed for acetaldehyde/alcohol injury is ______.
questions.exp: 'mnemonic : HESST' — Hypoxia, Endoplasmic reticulum stress, Superoxide, ↓SAM/↑SAH, Toxic effect of acetaldehyde. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: HESST — match — 1) Hypoxia 2) Endoplasmic reticulum stress 3) Superoxide … A) Mallory hyaline bodies B) Reactive oxygen species produced by Cyt P2E1 C) Mitochondrial injury in zone 3 (centrilobular hepatocyte)
questions.exp: Hypoxia: mitochondrial injury in Zone 3 (centrilobular); ER stress: Mallory hyaline bodies; Superoxide: ROS produced by Cyt P2E1. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: '↓SAM / ↑SAH' in the HESST list is linked to which factor labelled the most important pathogenic factor, and which drug is given as its Rx?
questions.exp: '↓SAM/↑SAH : ↑ TNFα most important pathogenic factor' and 'Rx : Pentoxifylline'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Fill up the chain printed for the toxic effect of acetaldehyde: ↑ NADH → ↓ ______ → ______ gut.
questions.exp: 'Toxic effect of acetaldehyde : ↑ NADH → ↓ glutathione → leaky gut'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Match — 1) Left image 2) Right image … A) Centrilobular necrosis, balloon degeneration, hepatocyte Mallory bodies B) Eosinophilic body inside hepatocyte: Mallory's hyaline bodies (endoplasmic reticulum stress)
questions.exp: Left caption: 'Eosinophilic body inside hepatocyte : Mallory's hyaline bodies (Endoplasmic reticulum stress)'. Right: 'Centrilobular necrosis, Balloon degeneration hepatocyte Mallory bodies'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Under the right micrograph, fatty liver disease is defined by fat in what proportion of hepatocytes, and what does fat pushing the nucleus to the periphery denote?
questions.exp: 'Fat in >5% Hepatocytes : Fatty liver disease. Fat pushes nucleus to periphery : macronodular.' (printed wording is macronodular). (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Laboratory features of alcoholic hepatitis — what is the first bullet and what enzyme range is given?
questions.exp: 'Neutrophilia : TC ↑' and 'Liver enzymes : 300 – 500 U/L'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: AST:ALT ratio — match — 1) > 2 : 1 2) > 3 : 1 … A) Highly suggestive of alcoholic hepatitis B) Likely alcoholic hepatitis
questions.exp: '>2:1 Likely Alcoholic hepatitis; >3:1 Highly suggestive of Alcoholic hepatitis'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Judge the remaining lab bullets: I S. albumin is a significant marker (positive acute-phase reactant). II PT/INR is raised. III MCV is raised (macrocytosis).
opts: I and II true, III false
I true; II and III false
I false; II and III true
questions.exp: 'S. Albumin : Not significant (Negative acute phase reactant)'; 'PT/INR : ↑'; 'MCV ↑ : macrocytosis'. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Thiamine depletion in alcoholics is drawn as inhibiting (−) two reactions. Which pair?
opts: Pyruvate → Acyl-CoA (blocked) and the transketolase reaction
questions.exp: 'Thiamine depletion (−) (−) → Pyruvate ✗→ Acyl-CoA ; Transketolase Reaction' (printed Acyl-CoA; the physiological product is acetyl-CoA). (Book p1027)

questions.sec: HESST adverse effects, acetaldehyde toxicity, micrographs, laboratory and clinical features
questions.q: Clinical features listed on this page — which is NOT printed?
questions.exp: Clinical features: Jaundice; P/A Soft, Painful; Hepatomegaly. (Book p1027)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Histopathological features of alcoholic hepatitis: where is the fatty infiltration located?
questions.exp: 'Centrilobular fatty infiltration (Zone III involvement)'. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Fill up the 'classical features' bullet: Ballooning degeneration / Alcoholic hyaline surrounding ______ infiltrate.
questions.exp: 'Ballooning degeneration/Alcoholic hyaline surrounding polymorphonuclear infiltrate (Classical features)'. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: The Note under histopathology says which viral hepatitis shows fatty liver-like changes / hepatic steatosis?
questions.exp: 'Note : Hepatitis C : fatty liver-like changes / hepatic steatosis.' (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: What does the trichrome micrograph on p1028 illustrate, per its caption?
opts: NASH: chicken-wire pericellular fibrosis of zone 3
NCPF: obliterative portal venopathy with sclerotic tracts
Alcoholic hepatitis: nodules with fibrous septation
Primary sclerosing cholangitis: concentric periductal fibrosis
questions.exp: Caption: 'Alcoholic hepatitis : Nodules with fibrous septation'. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Fill up the complications chain: Alcoholic hepatitis → Fulminant hepatitis / Decompensated → Encephalopathy + Coagulopathy (Portal HTN) → ↑ ______ → Death.
questions.exp: '… → Encephalopathy + Coagulopathy → ↑ ICT → Death', with 'Portal HTN' bracketed beneath. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Discriminant factor (DF) — state the formula and poor-prognosis cut-off exactly as printed.
opts: 4.6 × (PT patient − PT control) + S. bilirubin; poor prognosis ≥ 32
questions.exp: 'Discriminant factor : 4.6 × (PT(PE) − PT(C)) + S. bilirubin — Poor prognosis : ≥ 32'. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Prognostic scores — match — 1) MELD 2) Glasgow 3) Discriminant factor … A) ≥ 32 B) ≥ 9 C) ≥ 18
questions.exp: MELD ≥ 18; Glasgow ≥ 9; DF ≥ 32. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Treatment: what is the printed indication for steroid in alcoholic hepatitis, and the regimen?
opts: DF score ≥ 32; 1 mg/kg × 7 days tapering over 3 weeks
MELD ≥ 18; 1 mg/kg/day × 4 weeks tapering over 12 weeks
questions.exp: 'Indication to steroid : DF Score ≥ 32 → Start → 1 mg/kg × 7 days tapering over 3 weeks.' (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: Which of the following is NOT printed as 'unfit for steroid'?
questions.exp: Unfit for steroid: Sepsis; Renal failure; Ongoing GI disease. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Histopathology, complications chain, prognostic scores and treatment
questions.q: A binge drinker with DF 40 develops sepsis. Steroids are unsuitable. What alternative does the flowchart give, with its mechanism and dose?
opts: Pentoxifylline — PDE-5 inhibitor — 400 mg OD × 1 week
Pentoxifylline — inhibits TNF-α — 400 mg TDS × 4 weeks
questions.exp: Unfit for steroid → Pentoxifylline: 'Inhibits TNF-α; 400 mg TDS × 4 weeks'. (Book p1028)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Miscellaneous note: what is printed as the most common cause of cirrhosis?
questions.exp: 'm/c cause of cirrhosis : NASH'. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Causes of micronodular cirrhosis — which is NOT in the printed list?
questions.exp: Micronodular: Alcoholic hepatitis, Biliary cirrhosis, ICC, Cystic fibrosis, Budd Chiari syndrome, Hemochromatosis. Wilson's is the printed macronodular cause. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Which single cause is printed for macronodular cirrhosis?
questions.exp: 'Causes of macronodular cirrhosis : Wilson's disease'. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Fill up the mnemonic for microvesicular steatosis: 'Pretty visits ______ with Alcohol and ______'.
questions.exp: 'mnemonic : Pretty visits Jamaica with Alcohol and Acid.' (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Decode the mnemonic letters — match — 1) P 2) R 3) T 4) V … A) Tetracycline B) Reye's syndrome C) Valproate D) Pregnancy
questions.exp: Microvesicular column: Pregnancy, Reye's syndrome, Tetracycline, Valproate, Jamaican vomiting sickness, Alcoholic liver disease, Acid lipase deficiency. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Which condition is listed under MACROvesicular (not microvesicular) steatosis?
questions.exp: Macrovesicular: HCV, NASH, Wilson's disease. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Judge: I Alcoholic liver disease is placed in the microvesicular column. II HCV and NASH are in the macrovesicular column.
questions.exp: Alcoholic liver disease is in the microvesicular list (the 'Alcohol' of the mnemonic); HCV, NASH, Wilson's are macrovesicular. (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: How is Reye's syndrome characterised in the bullet after the table?
questions.exp: 'Reye's syndrome : Swollen mitochondria with reduced number.' (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Fill up: 'Nutmeg liver : Chronic ______ condition.'
questions.exp: 'Nutmeg liver : Chronic venous condition.' (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Mallory–Denk bodies are defined as what, and located where?
opts: Endoplasmic reticulum stress — eosinophilic inclusion bodies in hepatocytes
Mitochondrial stress — basophilic inclusions in Kupffer cells
Copper-bound protein — brown granules in bile ducts
questions.exp: 'Mallory denk bodies : Endoplasmic reticulum stress (Eosinophilic inclusion bodies) In hepatocytes.' (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Mallory–Denk bodies are 'seen in' a printed list. Which is NOT in that list?
questions.exp: Seen in: Wilson's, ICC, NASH, Cholestasis, Alcohol/Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, PBC, HCC. 'Not seen in HBV / HCV.' (Book p1029)

questions.sec: Miscellaneous: cirrhosis causes, micro vs macrovesicular steatosis, Reye's, nutmeg liver, Mallory-Denk bodies
questions.q: Judge: I Mallory–Denk bodies are seen in HCC. II They are seen in alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency. III They are seen in HBV.
opts: I true, II and III false
III true, I and II false
I and II true, III false
questions.exp: HCC and Alcohol/Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency are in the seen-in list; 'Not seen in HBV / HCV'. (Book p1029)

units.title: Dose thresholds, progression and alcohol metabolism
units.guide: 1 peg = 60 ml 40%; male 40–80 g (2 pegs), female 20–40 g (1 peg), 5 days/week × 15 years; alcoholic hepatitis mortality 70%, CDT best marker; 3–5 years to reversible fatty liver → cirrhosis (micro → macronodular, nucleus to periphery, HCC risk) or alcoholic hepatitis (binge); enzymes ALDH, CYP2E1, catalase; acetaldehyde toxic; ALDH polymorphism poor metaboliser prone to hepatitis.

units.title: HESST injury, histology images, laboratory and clinical features
units.guide: Hypoxia zone 3 mitochondria, ER stress Mallory hyaline, superoxide via CYP2E1, ↓SAM/↑SAH → TNF-α (pentoxifylline), acetaldehyde ↑NADH → ↓glutathione → leaky gut; fat >5% hepatocytes; neutrophilia, enzymes 300–500, AST:ALT >2:1 likely / >3:1 highly suggestive, albumin not significant, ↑PT/INR, ↑MCV, thiamine blocks pyruvate→acyl-CoA and transketolase; jaundice, soft painful abdomen, hepatomegaly.

units.title: Histopathology, complications, prognostic scores and treatment
units.guide: Zone III fatty infiltration; ballooning/alcoholic hyaline with PMN infiltrate; HCV steatosis note; nodules with fibrous septation; fulminant → encephalopathy + coagulopathy → ↑ICT → death; DF = 4.6 × (PT pt − control) + bilirubin ≥ 32, MELD ≥ 18, Glasgow ≥ 9; steroid 1 mg/kg × 7 days taper 3 weeks; unfit: sepsis, renal failure, GI disease → pentoxifylline 400 mg TDS × 4 weeks.

units.title: Miscellaneous notes: cirrhosis morphology, steatosis mnemonic, Reye's, nutmeg, Mallory–Denk
units.guide: NASH m/c cause of cirrhosis; micronodular list (alcohol, biliary, ICC, CF, Budd-Chiari, hemochromatosis) vs macronodular Wilson's; 'Pretty visits Jamaica with Alcohol and Acid' microvesicular vs HCV/NASH/Wilson's macrovesicular; Reye's swollen fewer mitochondria; nutmeg = chronic venous; Mallory-Denk ER-stress eosinophilic inclusions seen in Wilson's, ICC, NASH, cholestasis, alcohol/A1AT, PBC, HCC, not HBV/HCV.
